title: Dan Dan Noodles
subtitle: Sichuan noodles with spiced pork mince in a nutty, chilli-laced sauce
excerpt: Dan dan noodles come from Chengdu, where street vendors once carried pots of noodles on shoulder poles. The sauce is a balance of nutty peanut butter, soy, vinegar, and chilli. Make it once and you will not stop thinking about it.
sourceNotes: Dan dan mian is a traditional Sichuan street food. The name references the carrying poles (dan) used by vendors. Gochugaru is used here as an accessible substitute for Sichuan chilli flakes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead and stored in the fridge. The pork mince is best cooked fresh.

content.text: The peanut butter sauce thickens as it sits, so save a little pasta water to loosen it when mixing. Taste the sauce before adding it to the noodles and adjust the soy, vinegar, or chilli to your preference.

items.prepNote: finely grated, divided between pork and sauce

content.text: Make the sauce: whisk together the peanut butter, both soy sauces, sesame oil, gochugaru, rice vinegar, and 2 tablespoons of warm water until smooth. Taste and adjust the balance.
Cook the noodles in a large pot of boiling salted water according to the packet. Reserve a mugful of cooking water, then drain.
While the noodles cook, heat a splash of oil in a wok over high heat. Add the pork mince and cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and a little crispy.
Add the garlic and ginger to the pork. Stir-fry for 1 minute more. Season with a splash of light soy.
Add the sauce to the drained noodles and toss to coat. Loosen with pasta water as needed.
Divide into bowls. Top with the spiced pork and sliced spring onion. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: The sauce is too thick and pastes onto the noodles.
items.cause: Not enough pasta water was added to loosen it.
items.fix: Add pasta water a tablespoon at a time until it coats smoothly.

items.symptom: The pork has steamed rather than browned.
items.cause: The wok was not hot enough or the pan was crowded.
items.fix: Cook over maximum heat without stirring for 2 minutes first.

items.cause: The sauce needs more acid or salt.
items.fix: Add more rice vinegar or a small splash of soy, then taste again.
